ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.parent_proof_nl:
Let n be an integer with n > 1, and let x satisfy (n-1)/n <= x < 1. We prove the two floor identities separately.

First, fix any integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1. Since x < 1, we have kx < k. On the other hand, since x >= (n-1)/n,

kx >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.

Because k <= n-1 < n, we have k/n <= 1, hence k - k/n >= k - 1. Therefore

k - 1 <= kx < k.

The only integer in the half-open interval [k-1, k) is k-1, so by the definition of the floor function, floor(kx) = k - 1.

Now take k = n. From x < 1 we get nx < n, and from x >= (n-1)/n we get nx >= n-1. Thus

n - 1 <= nx < n.

Again by the definition of the floor function, floor(nx) = n - 1.

This proves that for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1, floor(kx) = k-1, and also floor(nx) = n-1.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2 (so that n-1 >= 1 and division by n is valid)
parent_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n at least 2 and every real x with (n-1)/n <= x < 1: for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1, floor of (k times x) equals k minus 1, and floor of (n times x) equals n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n at least 2
for all real numbers x with (n-1)/n <= x < 1
for all integers k with 1 <= k <= n-1
